title: Review: jmap-client pre-merge round 5
notes:
Maintainer risk: HIGH — Two issues (rustls-manual-roots breaking DefaultTransport, BlobIntegrityMismatch field naming) will generate immediate user-facing errors and confusing diagnostics. The AuthProvider silent-drop issue is a security surface. The SSE idle-timeout gap is a long-tail reliability issue.
Section 2: one efficiency finding filed (SSE CR normalization double-allocation). No O(n^2) patterns. All hot-path allocations bounded by 1 MiB cap.
Section 3: two elegance findings filed. No other control-flow or abstraction issues found that rise above stylistic preference.
Section 4: two readability findings filed. check_auth_status fully-qualified call in blob.rs is correct (static method). The SSE scan_from comment in client.rs is adequate.
Section 7: No Section 3/4 findings are pure taste with no engineering basis. Both elegance findings (11, 12) have concrete engineering justifications (allocation count, compile-time vs runtime safety). No opinion labels added.
Confidence: 15% chance of missed bug. Least confident flags: t47.1 (SSE invalid-byte drain behavior at the cap boundary — the scenario requires a pathological stream that is unlikely in practice but real in a hostile environment). Uncertainty driven by: inability to run the SSE stream code against a real adversarial server; the subscribe_events unfold closure is complex enough that edge-case interactions between raw_buf, buf, and scan_from may have additional issues not visible in static analysis. Would raise confidence if: a fuzz test were run against parse_sse_block and the unfold loop with arbitrary byte sequences including invalid UTF-8.
